interface.title: ATC Phase 4 — ASI-PLC Simulator
interface.field: Industrial control-system safety and cybersecurity (welding certification / PLC interlock logic)
interface.stage_of_work: Checking and exploring simulation results against a companion paper's reported results (Section VII-E / Table 8)
interface.what_it_is_for: Run a seeded Monte Carlo simulation of the ASI-PLC Compliance Bit state machine over a chosen mix of valid, non-compliant, MitM, replay and timeout scenarios, then check that it never permits a bad weld, that valid-weld latency stays under the 500 ms window, and how the scenarios split across PLC states.

data.note: There is no upload and no example-data button. Every scenario is generated in the app when Run simulation is clicked, using the sidebar seed and counts. Defaults are seed 2025 and 120/50/10/10/10. Changing any sidebar value clears the results until Run simulation is clicked again. Nothing can be downloaded: the downloads list stayed empty.

tree.general: Show that a safety interlock's decision logic never lets a non-compliant or tampered request through, and that its response time stays inside the allowed window
tree.specific: Reproduce the paper's 200-scenario ASI-PLC Monte Carlo result (seed 2025) and stress-test Compliance Bit fail-lock behaviour under other seeds and attack mixes

MitM rows end HARD_LOCK with STEP3_HMAC_INVALID. Replay rows end HARD_LOCK with STEP2_NONCE_REPLAY (rcv=10 ≤ last=10). Timeout rows end SOFT_LOCK with STEP1_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT (>500 ms), except idx 15 (497.4 ms) and idx 17 (495.4 ms), whose heartbeat stays under 500 ms and which end COMPLIANT with relay_on true. These boundary timeouts explain the 9/10 timeout detection in t4 and are not counted by the False permits card

features.name: Seeded scenario-mix Monte Carlo launcher
features.general: Set a random seed and how many cases of each category to generate, launch one run, and get a fresh result set. Editing any input throws away the old result so it cannot be mistaken for the new settings
features.specific: Sidebar number inputs (Random seed; Valid, Non-compliant, MitM, Replay, Timeout scenario counts) plus the Run simulation button that runs the ASI-PLC simulation. Changing any input clears the results back to the 'Adjust the controls…' prompt
steps: Type or step (+/−) a random seed
Set the count for each scenario category (Valid and Non-compliant step by 10; MitM, Replay and Timeout step by 5; typed values off the step are accepted, and there is no upper limit)
Press Run simulation
See the 'Simulation complete' banner and all result panels refresh
Change any input to clear the results, then run again
serves_tasks: Run the simulation with the published default settings and read the headline safety metrics
Repeat the baseline mix with a different random seed
Use a mix weighted towards attacks and faults and check that nothing unsafe gets through
Push one fault type to a large count to check the logic holds at scale
Reduce the normal cases so the fault cases show up in the limited record list, then set each fault type's outcome against the expected one

features.name: Safety-outcome metric card grid
features.general: A two-column block of headline counters that summarises a run in terms of safety errors (false accepts and false rejects) and how many cases were locked out, so a pass/fail check takes one glance. Two counters do not mean what their labels suggest, so check them against the per-state counts
features.specific: Six st.metric cards: Total scenarios, Valid results, False permits (relay on non-compliant weld), Soft lock count, False negatives, Hard lock events. False permits counts only non-compliant, MitM and replay cases and leaves out timeouts, so timeouts that end COMPLIANT with relay on are not flagged. Soft lock count shows the configured timeout count, not the SOFT_LOCK outcomes (Prototype_app.py:272-274, 351)
steps: Run a simulation
Read False permits and False negatives to check fail-lock behaviour, keeping in mind that timeouts are not counted
Compare Soft lock and Hard lock with the SOFT_LOCK and HARD_LOCK state counts, not only with the configured counts
Re-run with new settings and compare the cards
serves_tasks: Run the simulation with the published default settings and read the headline safety metrics
Use a mix weighted towards attacks and faults and check that nothing unsafe gets through
Push one fault type to a large count to check the logic holds at scale

features.name: Per-case decision trace table
features.general: Static table of individual cases giving the injected fault, final state, whether the output was switched on, latency and the reason it failed, so single decisions can be audited
features.specific: Scenario details table (idx, fault, state, relay_on, latency_ms, failures) for the first 30 scenarios. The failures column names the check that tripped (STEP1_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT, STEP2_NONCE_REPLAY, STEP3_HMAC_INVALID). Fault rows only appear when the valid count is below 30, because valid rows come first
